sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》负责商业和政策报道。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.zh: 拉加德、扎伊兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today, as the United States completes its military withdrawal from Afghanistan, the Taliban is seizing control of city after city across the country.
sentences.zh: 今天，随着美国完成从阿富汗的军事撤离，塔利班正在全国各地接管一个又一个城市。

sentences.en: Sabrina Tavernisi spoke with our colleague,
sentences.zh: 萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西采访了我们的同事，

sentences.en: Carlotta Gall, about the Taliban's strategy and why it's succeeding so quickly.
sentences.zh: 卡洛塔·加尔，探讨了塔利班的战略及其为何能如此迅速地取得成功。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday,
sentences.zh: 今天是星期二，

sentences.en: August 10th.
So, Carlotta, tell me what happened in Afghanistan over the weekend.
sentences.zh: 那么，卡洛塔，请告诉我们阿富汗周末发生了什么。

sentences.en: Well, after months of fighting, suddenly the Taliban have made a huge breakthrough this weekend with taking several big cities and suddenly toppling a lot of the north.
sentences.zh: 嗯，经过数月的战斗，塔利班在这个周末突然取得了巨大的突破，占领了几个大城市，并迅速推翻了北部地区的许多据点。

sentences.en: I think it's very serious and it's a very big move to take control of the country.
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常严重，是夺取国家控制权的一个重大举措。

sentences.en: So, Carlotta, what were those provincial capitals?
sentences.zh: 那么，卡洛塔，那些省会城市是哪些？

sentences.en: Walk us through exactly how the weekend played out.
sentences.zh: 请为我们详细梳理一下周末发生的情况。

sentences.en: So, a lot of provincial capitals have been under siege or under attack and there's been a bit of ebb and flow.
sentences.zh: 很多省会城市一直处于被围困或攻击的状态，局势时有起伏。

sentences.en: But on Friday, the Taliban took their first provincial capital.
sentences.zh: 但在周五，塔利班占领了他们的第一个省会城市。

sentences.en: We have two eyewitnesses confirming that the city of Zaranj in southwestern Afghanistan has fallen to the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 我们有两位目击者证实，阿富汗西南部的扎兰季市已经落入塔利班手中。

sentences.en: And it's a small place that not many people maybe know of called Zaranj on the southwestern border with
sentences.zh: 那是一个位于西南部与

sentences.en: Iran.
sentences.zh: 伊朗边境交界处的小地方，叫扎兰季，可能没多少人知道。

sentences.en: I tell you, the government say that they are on the outskirts, though, of Zaranj and battles continue.
sentences.zh: 我得说，政府方面表示他们仍在扎兰季郊外，战斗仍在继续。

sentences.en: And then very swiftly, in a completely different part of the country, in the north.
sentences.zh: 然后非常迅速地，在国家完全不同的另一个地区，即北部。

sentences.en: The Taliban now claiming a second provincial capital, Shibargan, is in their hands.
sentences.zh: 塔利班现在声称第二个省会城市希比尔甘已在他们手中。

sentences.en: They made a move on Shibargan, which is a medium-sized town, but an important province because it's always been anti-Taliban.
sentences.zh: 他们对希比尔甘采取了行动，这是一个中等规模的城镇，但作为一个省份很重要，因为它一直以来都是反塔利班的。

sentences.en: And then Sunday, three towns fell.
sentences.zh: 然后周日，三个城镇沦陷了。

sentences.en: The sun rising on what would become a historic day in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 太阳升起，开启了阿富汗历史上重要的一天。

sentences.en: First, the Taliban entered
sentences.zh: 首先，塔利班进入了

sentences.en: Kunduz.
sentences.zh: 昆都士。

sentences.en: Video released by the Taliban shows fighters retaking ground with excessive force, seizing key government buildings and reducing areas of the city to smoldering ruins.
sentences.zh: 塔利班发布的视频显示，武装分子以过度武力夺回地盘，占领了关键的政府大楼，并将城市部分地区化为冒烟的废墟。

sentences.en: That, I think, is the biggest shock because Kunduz is a major town, you know, more than a quarter of a million people.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是最大的冲击，因为昆都士是一个大城镇，你知道，有超过25万人口。

sentences.en: Breadbasket of Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗的粮仓。

sentences.en: And then now, Monday evening, we're hearing reports that a sixth province is falling.
sentences.zh: 现在是周一晚上，我们收到报告称第六个省份正在沦陷。

sentences.en: Samangan, which is actually a very strategic, also northern province, but it's on the main road that links the north to Kabul.
sentences.zh: 萨曼甘，这实际上也是一个非常具有战略意义的北部省份，但它位于连接北部到喀布尔的主干道上。

sentences.en: So a huge change.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个巨大的变化。

sentences.en: Suddenly, the Taliban has upped its gear and it's going for the cities, populated areas in different parts of the country.
sentences.zh: 塔利班突然加快了步伐，开始进攻全国不同地区的人口稠密城市。

sentences.en: So I think it's a huge blow for the government.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这对政府来说是一个巨大的打击。

sentences.en: So that's six cities in four days.
sentences.zh: 所以那是四天内六座城市。

sentences.en: I mean, that seems really faSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这看起来真的很快。

sentences.en: Was this a shock to you or to Afghans?
sentences.zh: 这对你或阿富汗人来说是一个冲击吗？

sentences.en: Were you expecting this?
sentences.zh: 你预料到了吗？

sentences.en: You know, I've learned over years of reporting from Afghanistan never to predict and never to really expect.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在阿富汗报道多年后，我学会了永远不要预测，也永远不要抱有太高的期望。

sentences.en: So was I expecting?
sentences.zh: 所以我预料到了吗？

sentences.en: I was fearing something like this would happen.
sentences.zh: 我一直担心会发生这样的事情。

sentences.en: But of course, it's a shock.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这依然是一个冲击。

sentences.en: And I think for the Afghan people that I'm messaging with and in touch with, they're appalled.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于我正在联系和交流的阿富汗人民来说，他们感到震惊。

sentences.en: They're frightened.
sentences.zh: 他们感到恐惧。

sentences.en: A lot of them are on the move and they're close to despair.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人正在逃离，濒临绝望。

sentences.en: And then don't forget, it's not just those towns because a lot of the other towns are under siege.
sentences.zh: 而且别忘了，不仅仅是那些城镇，因为许多其他城镇也处于被围困状态。

sentences.en: So, of course, you imagine if you're sitting in a provincial capital that's under shell fire and you hear other major cities have fallen.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，你可以想象如果你身处一个正遭受炮火袭击的省会城市，又听说其他主要城市已经沦陷。

sentences.en: It's very, very harsh on the morale, I think, of everyone in the country.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对全国每个人的士气都是非常、非常沉重的打击。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, Carlotta, how does all of this fit into the broader Taliban military strategy?
sentences.zh: 那么，卡洛塔，这一切如何融入塔利班更广泛的军事战略中？

sentences.en: This is altogether an escalation of their main strategy,
sentences.zh: 这完全是他们主要战略的升级，

sentences.en: which we've seen for the last two years since they made a deal with the Americans for the American withdrawal from Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 自他们与美国达成撤军协议以来的过去两年里，我们一直看到这一点。

sentences.en: The Taliban had agreed then not to attack the U.S.
sentences.zh: 塔利班当时同意不攻击美国

sentences.en: forces and not to attack cities.
sentences.zh: 军队，也不攻击城市。

sentences.en: But they did start seizing territory and they cleared up and took a lot of rural districts.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实开始夺取领土，并清理并占领了许多农村地区。

sentences.en: And then what was interesting was they seized a lot of the border posts.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，他们占领了许多边境哨所。

sentences.en: And that was clearly an important strategic aim because they can use leverage against the government.
sentences.zh: 这显然是一个重要的战略目标，因为他们可以利用这一点对政府施压。

sentences.en: They seized the government's lucrative customs posts.
sentences.zh: 他们占领了政府利润丰厚的海关哨所。

sentences.en: They seized a bank and got lots of cash.
sentences.zh: 他们抢劫了一家银行，获得了大量现金。

sentences.en: They showed off the cash that they seized in Herat.
sentences.zh: 他们在赫拉特炫耀了他们抢来的现金。

sentences.en: And then they moved on the provincial capitals this weekend.
sentences.zh: 然后这个周末他们开始进攻省会城市。

sentences.en: And so what it looks like is they've got this strategy to steadily take all the outer rim of the country, the border posts, the entry points, the provinces around the edges,
sentences.zh: 所以看起来他们的战略是稳步占领该国的所有外围地区、边境哨所、入境点、边缘省份，

sentences.en: and then slowly encroach on the center and, I think, do a stranglehold on the capital, Kabul.
sentences.zh: 然后慢慢向中心推进，我认为，对首都喀布尔形成扼杀。

sentences.en: So, Carlotta, you've talked a little bit about this, but what does it feel like on the ground as the Taliban starts to take over these provincial cities?
sentences.zh: 那么，卡洛塔，你已经谈到了一些，但当塔利班开始接管这些省会城市时，当地的感觉如何？

sentences.en: Well, it's been very grim.
sentences.zh: 嗯，情况非常严峻。

sentences.en: What we know from the rural areas or the suburbs of the cities is that they've come in, they occupy houses, they push people out and take over their house.
sentences.zh: 我们从农村地区或城市郊区了解到的情况是，他们进来了，占据房屋，把人们赶出去并接管他们的房子。

sentences.en: They lay IEDs and antipersonnel mines all over the village, all over the fields.
sentences.zh: 他们在村庄和田野里到处埋设简易爆炸装置和杀伤性地雷。

sentences.en: They dig tunnels because up until now they've been worried about a counterattack by the government.
sentences.zh: 他们挖掘地道，因为到目前为止他们一直担心政府的反击。

sentences.en: They closed all the girls' schools.
sentences.zh: 他们关闭了所有的女子学校。

sentences.en: I know that from, you know, in Kandahar, they even stop people using their cell phones.
sentences.zh: 我知道在坎大哈，他们甚至禁止人们使用手机。

sentences.en: So a lot of the old rules and, of course, Sharia law, so women aren't allowed out without a male relative.
sentences.zh: 所以很多旧规则，当然还有伊斯兰教法，所以女性没有男性亲属陪同不得外出。

sentences.en: Men, I think, even being told to grow beards again.
sentences.zh: 我想，男性甚至被告知要重新留胡子。

sentences.en: And we've seen some signs of whippings and so the old extreme rule of the Taliban under Sharia law.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到了一些鞭刑的迹象，这就是塔利班在伊斯兰教法下那种古老的极端统治。

sentences.en: What is most alarming that we've seen is certainly in one town of Spinbaldak,
sentences.zh: 我们看到的最令人担忧的事情无疑是在斯平布尔达克镇，

sentences.en: despite agreements where they asked the police forces or the local militia to surrender and be allowed to go free,
sentences.zh: 尽管有协议要求警察部队或当地民兵投降并获准自由离开，

sentences.en: they then did go door to door and pull out people who'd worked with the government, particularly security forces, and they executed 44 people, we know for sure.
sentences.zh: 但他们随后挨家挨户搜查，把那些曾与政府合作的人，特别是安全部队人员拉出来，我们确定他们处决了44人。

sentences.en: There's a lot of others missing.
sentences.zh: 还有许多人失踪。

sentences.en: So that was a very sinister harbinger of what might happen on a larger scale.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常险恶的预兆，预示着更大规模的事情可能会发生。

sentences.en: So they're executing people who were working with the Afghan government as well as the United States.
sentences.zh: 所以他们也在处决那些与阿富汗政府以及美国合作的人？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we've had in different provinces, we've had the president's spokesperson was killed on Friday.
sentences.zh: 在不同的省份，周五总统的发言人被杀了。

sentences.en: We've had a headmaster from a central province was killed in a place overrun by the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 在中部省份，一位校长在塔利班占领的地方被杀。

sentences.en: We've had a schoolteacher.
sentences.zh: 还有一位学校老师。

sentences.en: So, of course, people are very frightened, including in Kabul, where the Taliban haven't come near yet,
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，人们非常害怕，包括在喀布尔，虽然塔利班还没有靠近，

sentences.en: but they know well that anyone connected to the government or to foreign organizations is going to be in danger.
sentences.zh: 但他们很清楚，任何与政府或外国组织有联系的人都会处于危险之中。

sentences.en: So there's a great feeling of dread.
sentences.zh: 所以有一种巨大的恐惧感。

sentences.en: And then a lot of the women, of course, are asking, I mean, friends and acquaintances are saying, will we be allowed to work?
sentences.zh: 当然，许多女性在问，我的朋友和熟人在说，我们还能被允许工作吗？

sentences.en: Will we be allowed to go out of the house?
sentences.zh: 我们还能被允许走出家门吗？

sentences.en: So I think for all women across the board, there's great concern.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为对于所有女性来说，普遍存在着巨大的担忧。

sentences.en: And then I think for ordinary Afghans, it's this fighting.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于普通阿富汗人来说，就是这种战斗。

sentences.en: You know, if they're going to struggle to fight for every city and there's going to be a big fight, you know, how many people are going to get killed and injured?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果他们要为每一座城市而战，而且会有大规模的战斗，你知道，会有多少人伤亡？

sentences.en: I mean, this is an incredibly fraught and complicated and really dire situation for a lot of Afghans.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这对许多阿富汗人来说是一个极其紧张、复杂且真正可怕的局面。

sentences.en: But I would imagine that people are kind of making the calculation about sort of where power is going to be and what might be safe for their families.
sentences.zh: 但我可以想象，人们正在权衡权力将走向何方，以及对他们的家庭来说什么可能是安全的。

sentences.en: So are people at all supportive of the Taliban?
sentences.zh: 那么人们是否支持塔利班？

sentences.en: I mean, how are ordinary Afghans kind of responding to this?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，普通阿富汗人是如何应对的？

sentences.en: You're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: Because when I say all Afghans, you know, are terrified, I think they are because they've seen so much violence.
sentences.zh: 因为当我提到所有阿富汗人都感到恐惧时，我认为他们确实如此，因为他们目睹了太多的暴力。

sentences.en: They know to expect the worSt.
sentences.zh: 他们知道要做好最坏的打算。

sentences.en: But there are already, of course, people reaching out to the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 但当然，已经有人开始接触塔利班了。

sentences.en: And Afghans have always learned how to survive is you bend with the wind.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗人一直学会了如何生存，那就是随风倒。

sentences.en: So a lot of them are already doing that.
sentences.zh: 所以他们中的许多人已经在这么做了。

sentences.en: You actually see people raising the Taliban flag in cities, talking about them in the mosques.
sentences.zh: 你实际上看到人们在城市里升起塔利班旗帜，在清真寺里谈论他们。

sentences.en: There's even some people who are going on these television chat shows and who are supporting the return of Sharia,
sentences.zh: 甚至有些人参加电视访谈节目，支持伊斯兰教法的回归，

sentences.en: welcoming the departure of the foreign forces.
sentences.zh: 欢迎外国军队的离开。

sentences.en: And this is what we heard actually in Kunduz.
sentences.zh: 这实际上就是我们在昆都士听到的。

sentences.en: The crowds were cheering the Taliban because that's what you do.
sentences.zh: 人群在为塔利班欢呼，因为你只能这样做。

sentences.en: You cheer the conqueror because you've got to go and live under them.
sentences.zh: 你为征服者欢呼，因为你必须在他们的统治下生活。

sentences.en: So I know so many of them don't want the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道他们中很多人并不想要塔利班。

sentences.en: They'd prefer a free society and a safe society.
sentences.zh: 他们更喜欢一个自由和安全的社会。

sentences.en: But if the Taliban's coming, they know how to survive.
sentences.zh: 但如果塔利班来了，他们知道如何生存。

sentences.en: They'll just keep their mouths shut and their heads down.
sentences.zh: 他们只会闭嘴，低调行事。

sentences.en: People will just bend with the wind, as it were.
sentences.zh: 人们会随风倒，正如人们所说的那样。

sentences.en: So, Carlotta, at this point, how significant are these Taliban seizures?
sentences.zh: 那么，卡洛塔，在这一点上，塔利班的这些占领有多重要？

sentences.en: Like how much control has the Afghan government actually lost?
sentences.zh: 阿富汗政府实际上失去了多少控制权？

sentences.en: I mean, this is five, maybe six of 30 plus provinces.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是30多个省中的五个，也许是六个。

sentences.en: So it's still a small percentage.
sentences.zh: 所以这仍然是一个很小的比例。

sentences.en: But what has happened, of course, is they've now taken big provincial towns on either side of Mazar-e-Sharif, which is the main town in the north.
sentences.zh: 但当然，发生的事情是他们现在占领了北部主要城镇马扎里沙里夫两侧的大型省会城镇。

sentences.en: So they now are in a very good position to move on it from two sides.
sentences.zh: 所以他们现在处于一个非常有利的位置，可以从两侧向它推进。

sentences.en: And if they've taken Samangan, they've cut the main road.
sentences.zh: 如果他们占领了萨曼甘，他们就切断了主干道。

sentences.en: So strategically, they're really gaining.
sentences.zh: 所以在战略上，他们确实在获益。

sentences.en: And then in the south, the two big cities.
sentences.zh: 然后在南部，有两座大城市。

sentences.en: So really, they must be feeling they're on a roll.
sentences.zh: 所以真的，他们一定感觉自己势不可挡。

sentences.en: And this is, I think, very significant because it'll give them a huge boost to move further.
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常重要，因为它将给他们进一步行动带来巨大的推动力。

sentences.en: And, Carlotta, is your eye at this point, as you analyze this and watch this, on the capital?
sentences.zh: 卡洛塔，当你分析和观察这一切时，你的目光是否聚焦在首都？

sentences.en: How are you understanding Kabul right now?
sentences.zh: 你现在如何看待喀布尔？

sentences.en: It's the ultimate prize, obviously.
sentences.zh: 显然，这是终极奖品。

sentences.en: The palace is there.
sentences.zh: 宫殿在那里。

sentences.en: The presidential palace is there.
sentences.zh: 总统府在那里。

sentences.en: All the embassies, the major airport.
sentences.zh: 所有的使馆，主要机场。

sentences.en: And it's, you know, a beautiful, famous, historic city.
sentences.zh: 而且它是一个美丽、著名、历史悠久的城市。

sentences.en: I just cannot predict what will happen and how quickly and soon they can put a strangle on it.
sentences.zh: 我无法预测会发生什么，以及他们能多快、多早对它形成扼杀。

sentences.en: You know, we've had battles for years over Kabul in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，过去我们曾为喀布尔进行了多年的战斗。

sentences.en: It won't be easy and it might be where the government draws the line and makes a stand.
sentences.zh: 这不会容易，这可能是政府划定界限并进行抵抗的地方。

sentences.en: And, of course, you know, there's a lot of people in Kabul, civilians as well as security forces, who oppose the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 当然，你知道，喀布尔有很多人，包括平民和安全部队，他们反对塔利班。

sentences.en: So would be expected to put up a fight.
sentences.zh: 所以预计会进行反抗。

sentences.en: And so we don't know what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: But I think you can definitely say the Taliban is going to make a move towards Kabul.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你可以肯定地说，塔利班将向喀布尔采取行动。

sentences.en: And that's very dramatic because you've got the huge American embassy with hundreds of Marines still there guarding the embassy and a NATO civilian office.
sentences.zh: 这非常戏剧性，因为那里有巨大的美国大使馆，仍有数百名海军陆战队员守卫着大使馆，还有一个北约文职办公室。

sentences.en: You've got Turkish troops in the airport.
sentences.zh: 机场里有土耳其军队。

sentences.en: You've got really quite a mix there of a big capital city of four million people.
sentences.zh: 那里确实是一个拥有四百万人口的大都市，情况非常复杂。

sentences.en: So that's the ultimate prize.
sentences.zh: 那便是终极奖赏。

sentences.en: But it's also the most worrying place because that's where there could be an ultimate, really dreadful confrontation.
sentences.zh: 但那也是最令人担忧的地方，因为那里可能会发生一场终极的、极其可怕的对抗。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重塑者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在黑胶唱片时代做夜店DJ的时候，你每天也要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个活生生的、快闪式的博物馆，陈列着那些精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重塑者》吧。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》App？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁版？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能让你免费试用一个月，且无需绑定信用卡，去探索《纽约时报》呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 首次下载《纽约时报》App，首月免费。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《纽约时报》的订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订阅者，今天就下载《纽约时报》App，获取30天的免费阅读权限。

sentences.en: So, Carlotta, I want to come back to this idea of shock and being surprised that this is all happening.
sentences.zh: 卡洛塔，我想回到关于“震惊”以及对这一切正在发生感到意外的观点上。

sentences.en: How did the Americans not see this coming?
sentences.zh: 美国人怎么会没预见到这一点？

sentences.en: I mean, there had been three presidents, Obama, Trump, and now Biden, talking about how to pull out, when to pull out, the challenges of ending this war.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，已经有三任总统——奥巴马、特朗普，现在是拜登——都在讨论如何撤军、何时撤军，以及结束这场战争所面临的挑战。

sentences.en: I mean, is there a sense that they knew at some level that this was inevitable?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们是否在某种程度上意识到这是不可避免的？

sentences.en: My feeling is they definitely knew.
sentences.zh: 我的感觉是他们绝对知道。

sentences.en: I mean, certainly we've heard over the weekend the Biden administration saying the withdrawal is still on track.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们周末听到了拜登政府的表态，称撤军仍在按计划进行。

sentences.en: There's no change to his plan.
sentences.zh: 他的计划没有任何改变。

sentences.en: And so I think they all say, certainly American officials say to us that they're surprised, that they didn't expect the government to be so weak or to lose territory so quickly.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他们都这么说，美国官员当然对我们说他们感到惊讶，他们没想到政府会如此软弱，或者失去领土的速度会如此之快。

sentences.en: But ultimately, they did know because they've been talking to the Taliban for three years now for this peace deal and in the agreement for the American withdrawal.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，他们是知道的，因为他们已经与塔利班就这份和平协议和美国撤军协议进行了三年的谈判。

sentences.en: And I think if you talk to any of the Afghan negotiators, they say it's very clear when you talk to the Taliban that they have no intention of really dealing peace.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，如果你和任何一位阿富汗谈判代表交谈，他们会说，当你与塔利班交谈时，很明显他们根本无意真正达成和平。

sentences.en: They want power.
sentences.zh: 他们想要的是权力。

sentences.en: And so I'm sure the American administration knows this, but they've decided to pull out.
sentences.zh: 所以我相信美国政府知道这一点，但他们还是决定撤军。

sentences.en: And however grim it is, they're going to stick with the course.
sentences.zh: 无论情况多么严峻，他们都会坚持到底。

sentences.en: Does the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国有计划在任何时候介入吗？

sentences.en: have a plan to step in at any point?
sentences.zh: 美国的战略是什么？

sentences.en: What's the U.S.'s strategy here?
sentences.zh: 美国的战略是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, it doesn't look like it.
sentences.zh: 是的，看起来并没有。

sentences.en: The Biden administration comment is that the withdrawal continues and the withdrawal is intended to be full.
sentences.zh: 拜登政府的说法是撤军继续进行，而且撤军旨在全面完成。

sentences.en: What they have walked back a little bit on is airstrikes.
sentences.zh: 他们稍微有所退让的是空袭方面。

sentences.en: Although they've taken all the American fighter planes out and all the drones, they have redeployed them from Doha, where they are in the Gulf.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们已经撤走了所有美国战斗机和无人机，但他们已将它们从多哈重新部署到了海湾地区。

sentences.en: So they're flying long distances, but they are coming to the aid of some of the Afghan forces.
sentences.zh: 所以它们在进行长距离飞行，但它们确实在为一些阿富汗部队提供支援。

sentences.en: And particularly, we've seen there's been bombing in Lashkargar, which is an important strategic place, and Kandahar.
sentences.zh: 特别是我们看到拉什卡尔加——一个重要的战略要地——和坎大哈发生了轰炸。

sentences.en: So I think they're trying to stall Taliban advances on some major cities, lessen the disaster.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他们正试图阻滞塔利班在一些主要城市的推进，以减轻灾难。

sentences.en: But I'm not sure they're in any position at this stage to reverse some of these Taliban advances.
sentences.zh: 但我并不确定他们现阶段是否有能力扭转塔利班的一些攻势。

sentences.en: So it's really, I think, now perhaps face-saving to make it not such a disaster and so rapid, because that inevitably will reflect on Washington's decision to leave.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，现在或许是为了挽回颜面，让局面不至于那么灾难性且迅速崩溃，因为这不可避免地会反映出华盛顿撤军决定的后果。

sentences.en: Where does this leave the Afghan government?
sentences.zh: 这让阿富汗政府处于什么境地？

sentences.en: Well, they're really struggling, I think.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为他们真的在苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: They say they're actually planning to retake all these places, so they're putting on a brave front.
sentences.zh: 他们说他们实际上计划夺回所有这些地方，所以他们表现得很勇敢。

sentences.en: But when you talk to them personally, officials are very worried.
sentences.zh: 但当你私下与他们交谈时，官员们非常担心。

sentences.en: They say it's very bad.
sentences.zh: 他们说情况非常糟糕。

sentences.en: They're well aware of the suffering of the people.
sentences.zh: 他们非常清楚人民所遭受的苦难。

sentences.en: So it's looking very grim.
sentences.zh: 所以情况看起来非常严峻。

sentences.en: I think they're struggling on the military front, you know, for supply.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们在军事前线，你知道，在补给方面正陷入困境。

sentences.en: It's, I think, extremely tough for them.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对他们来说极其艰难。

sentences.en: And I think they feel betrayed by the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他们感到被西方背叛了。

sentences.en: You know, so many Afghans worked for Western organizations or took them at their word and got educated and tried to open businesses.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这么多阿富汗人为西方组织工作，或者相信了他们的话，接受了教育，并尝试开办企业。

sentences.en: Whatever they did, you know, they were doing it because they believed in the future.
sentences.zh: 无论他们做了什么，你知道，他们这样做是因为他们相信未来。

sentences.en: And so I think now they're feeling very bereft and some are feeling very angry and feel betrayed.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为现在他们感到非常被剥夺，有些人感到非常愤怒，感到被背叛了。

sentences.en: The government won't say it, but the people will say it to you.
sentences.zh: 政府不会说出来，但民众会告诉你。

sentences.en: So, Carlotta, the government is saying they're going to retake these cities.
sentences.zh: 那么，卡洛塔，政府声称他们将夺回这些城市。

sentences.en: But what we're really seeing right now is that the Afghan military just isn't very evenly matched.
sentences.zh: 但我们现在真正看到的是，阿富汗军队的实力并不均衡。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: It's varied, actually.
sentences.zh: 实际上情况各异。

sentences.en: I mean, certainly there are places where they've pulled out very rapidly and surprisingly, like these last towns in the last few days.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当然有些地方他们撤退得非常迅速且令人惊讶，比如过去几天里的这些城镇。

sentences.en: But in the South, it's interesting, there's been weeks of fighting, very heavy fighting in two big cities, Kandahar and Lashkagar.
sentences.zh: 但在南部，有趣的是，在坎大哈和拉什卡尔加这两个大城市已经进行了数周的激战，非常激烈的战斗。

sentences.en: And you see there's a young general who's become very famous in Afghanistan, General Sami Sadat.
sentences.zh: 你看到有一位年轻的将军在阿富汗变得非常出名，萨米·萨达特将军。

sentences.en: He's Afghan National Army trained, you know, educated and trained since 9-11.
sentences.zh: 他是阿富汗国民军训练出来的，你知道，自9·11事件以来受过教育和训练。

sentences.en: And he's the head of the corps down there.
sentences.zh: 他是那里的军团指挥官。

sentences.en: And he's, you know, he's formidable and he's managed to repel multiple attacks by the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 他，你知道，他很强大，并且成功击退了塔利班的多次进攻。

sentences.en: And they've been fighting inside the city, right up close to the governor's palace.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在城内战斗，就在省长官邸附近。

sentences.en: And he's still hanging in there and seems to have been able to repel them.
sentences.zh: 他仍然坚持在那里，似乎已经能够击退他们。

sentences.en: And so that shows that I think there are people who are capable of fighting and still determined to fight.
sentences.zh: 这表明我认为确实有人有能力战斗，并且仍然决心战斗。

sentences.en: So there are some holdouts, at least for now, it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来至少目前还有一些坚守者。

sentences.en: Yes, there certainly are.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实有。

sentences.en: This is kind of a crystal ball kind of question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个类似水晶球预测的问题。

sentences.en: But, you know, you've been covering Afghanistan for 30 years.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，你报道阿富汗已经30年了。

sentences.en: In your mind, where does it go from here?
sentences.zh: 在你看来，接下来会怎样？

sentences.en: What are we seeing right now?
sentences.zh: 我们现在看到了什么？

sentences.en: What does it mean?
sentences.zh: 这意味着什么？

sentences.en: It's very hard to predict Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 预测阿富汗的情况非常困难。

sentences.en: Afghanistan, it always surprises you.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗总是让你感到意外。

sentences.en: And I'm very careful because you're usually wrong if you try and predict on Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 而且我非常谨慎，因为如果你试图预测阿富汗，通常都会出错。

sentences.en: But, I mean, I think there's two scenarios.
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，我认为有两种可能。

sentences.en: The Taliban could well take control, whether they take it all by fighting or they achieve enough territory to do a stranglehold on the capital.
sentences.zh: 塔利班很可能夺取控制权，无论是通过战斗夺取全部，还是获得足够的领土来扼杀首都。

sentences.en: And then they perhaps do some sort of agreement or coup or anything is possible.
sentences.zh: 然后他们可能会达成某种协议或发动政变，一切皆有可能。

sentences.en: But I think that's what the Taliban are set on.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这就是塔利班的目标。

sentences.en: They would like to take Kabul and take the whole country.
sentences.zh: 他们想夺取喀布尔，夺取整个国家。

sentences.en: And if they do, then I think we will see a fundamentalist, very extreme regime back in power.
sentences.zh: 如果他们做到了，那么我认为我们将看到一个原教旨主义的、非常极端的政权重新掌权。

sentences.en: And I think we will see Afghanistan slide backwards in terms of democracy and human rights and freedoMs.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们将看到阿富汗在民主、人权和自由方面倒退。

sentences.en: Or you could get what everyone has been hoping, you know, the international communities hope for, is some kind of peace deal where there's a sharing of power.
sentences.zh: 或者你可能会得到每个人都希望的结果，你知道，国际社会的希望，即某种权力分享的和平协议。

sentences.en: Anyone that I know who has studied the Taliban or knows the Taliban, just say that's not on the cards with the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 任何我认识的研究过塔利班或了解塔利班的人，都说这在塔利班那里是不可能的。

sentences.en: So I just don't see that happening.
sentences.zh: 所以我根本看不出这会发生。

sentences.en: So it's looking very grim, I think, very grim for anyone who believed in these last two decades of progress for Afghanistan and, you know, for all its faults.
sentences.zh: 所以情况看起来非常严峻，我认为，对于任何相信过去二十年阿富汗取得进步的人来说，无论它有什么缺陷，情况都非常严峻。

sentences.en: And I wrote about a lot of them, you know, all the civilian casualties, all the failures of the international effort there, the mistakes made and so on.
sentences.zh: 我写过很多关于这些的内容，你知道，所有的平民伤亡，国际努力在那里的所有失败，所犯的错误等等。

sentences.en: And I think the Afghans made huge strides, you know, they did have democracy, they did have freedoMs.
sentences.zh: 我认为阿富汗人取得了巨大的进步，你知道，他们确实拥有了民主，确实拥有了自由。

sentences.en: You know, you saw whole generations getting educated.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你看到整整一代人接受了教育。

sentences.en: I mean, all these kids who only grew up after 9-11, you know, have managed to make it to college.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，所有这些只在9·11之后长大的孩子，你知道，都成功上了大学。

sentences.en: And they've done a lot of rebuilding.
sentences.zh: 他们做了很多重建工作。

sentences.en: And that's what's very distressing already.
sentences.zh: 而这正是已经非常令人痛苦的事情。

sentences.en: You see the Taliban destroying so much of what was built in the last 10, 20 years.
sentences.zh: 你看到塔利班正在摧毁过去10年、20年里建立的那么多东西。

sentences.en: You know, roads, district buildings, you know, customs houses and asphalt roads they're just digging up because they were laid by the Americans, they say, and we don't need these.
sentences.zh: 你知道，道路、地区建筑、你知道，海关大楼和沥青路，他们只是因为这些是美国人铺设的就将其挖掉，他们说，我们不需要这些。

sentences.en: So really some wanton destruction, which just it's maddening to see because there's a lot of effort that went into all that.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是一些肆意的破坏，看到这些真是令人抓狂，因为所有这些都投入了巨大的努力。

sentences.en: Let me ask this.
sentences.zh: 让我问这个问题。

sentences.en: What do Afghans want?
sentences.zh: 阿富汗人想要什么？

sentences.en: I think every Afghan will tell you they want peace.
sentences.zh: 我想每个阿富汗人都会告诉你他们想要和平。

sentences.en: They want peace and security.
sentences.zh: 他们想要和平与安全。

sentences.en: They want to be able to get their fruit to market.
sentences.zh: 他们希望能够把水果运到市场。

sentences.en: They want to raise their kids.
sentences.zh: 他们想要抚养孩子。

sentences.en: The people who are appealing to me to help to get out are usually saying they're doing it for their children, you know, especially their girls.
sentences.zh: 那些恳求我帮助他们离开的人通常说他们这样做是为了孩子，你知道，尤其是他们的女儿。

sentences.en: They can't bear to see them have to sit at home and be robbed of an education just because they're girls.
sentences.zh: 他们无法忍受看到她们不得不坐在家里，仅仅因为是女孩就被剥夺了受教育的机会。

sentences.en: So that's the main thing people want.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是人们最想要的东西。

sentences.en: The kids want to go to school.
sentences.zh: 孩子们想上学。

sentences.en: The families want to be able to earn a living and have safety.
sentences.zh: 家庭希望能够谋生并获得安全。

sentences.en: And so a Taliban win could bring a forced peace.
sentences.zh: 所以塔利班的胜利可能会带来一种强迫的和平。

sentences.en: But most people are predicting that they won't because they're trying to take control by force.
sentences.zh: 但大多数人预测他们不会，因为他们正试图通过武力夺取控制权。

sentences.en: And so there will be inevitably resistance and opposition.
sentences.zh: 因此不可避免地会有抵抗和反对。

sentences.en: And so the war will go on.
sentences.zh: 所以战争将会继续。

sentences.en: There's no doubt.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: The Afghans have been fighting for 40 years and they're probably going to fight for many more.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗人已经战斗了40年，他们很可能会继续战斗很多年。

sentences.en: Carlotta, thank you.
sentences.zh: 卡洛塔，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Pleasure.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他内容。

sentences.en: A major United Nations report on climate change written by hundreds of scientists has found that the world can no longer stop global warming from intensifying over the next 30 years.
sentences.zh: 一份由数百名科学家撰写的关于气候变化的重大联合国报告发现，世界已无法阻止全球变暖在未来30年内加剧。

sentences.en: The report is a damning indictment of an unwillingness to curb fossil fuel emissions that has locked in extreme weather for the next several decades.
sentences.zh: 这份报告是对抑制化石燃料排放意愿不足的严厉控诉，这种不足已经锁定了未来几十年的极端天气。

sentences.en: And the Democratic budget will be the most significant legislation for American families since the era of the New Deal and the Great Society.
sentences.zh: 民主党的预算案将是自“新政”和“伟大社会”时代以来对美国家庭最重要的立法。

sentences.en: On Monday, congressional Democrats released a proposed $3.5 trillion budget plan that would represent a historic expansion of the social safety net.
sentences.zh: 周一，国会民主党人公布了一项拟议的3.5万亿美元预算计划，这将代表社会安全网的历史性扩张。

sentences.en: It is big, bold change.
sentences.zh: 这是重大、大胆的变革。

sentences.en: The kind of change America thirsts for.
sentences.zh: 美国所渴望的那种变革。

sentences.en: The budget plan is a follow-up to the proposed bipartisan infrastructure bill that is expected to pass this morning.
sentences.zh: 该预算计划是拟议中的两党基础设施法案的后续，预计将于今天上午通过。

sentences.en: The budget plan would raise spending on health care, child care and elder care, education and climate change,
sentences.zh: 该预算计划将增加在医疗保健、儿童保育和老年护理、教育和气候变化方面的支出，

sentences.en: and pay for it all by raising taxes on the wealthy, corporations and large inheritances.
sentences.zh: 并通过提高对富人、企业和巨额遗产的税收来支付所有费用。

sentences.en: Democrats hoped to pass the budget plan through a process that would require a simple majority in the Senate and therefore bypass a Republican filibuster.
sentences.zh: 民主党人希望通过一个在参议院只需简单多数票即可通过的程序来通过该预算计划，从而绕过共和党的阻挠议事。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Luke Vanderpluk, Lindsay Garrison and Sidney Harper, with help from Eric Krupke and Claire Tennisgetter.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由卢克·范德普鲁克、林赛·加里森和西德尼·哈珀制作，埃里克·克鲁普克和克莱尔·坦尼斯盖特提供了帮助。

sentences.en: It was edited by M.J.
sentences.zh: 由M.J.戴维斯-林恩编辑，克里斯·伍德担任工程设计，并包含玛丽安·洛萨诺的原创音乐。

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn, engineered by Chris Wood, and contains original music by Marian Lozano.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严格控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 当选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人激动的斗争之中。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 在《地铁》的最新一集中，和我一起，萨拉·凯尼格，讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 在任何你获取播客的地方收听。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在任何你获取播客的地方收听。
